title: orchestrator
definition: A control plane component that schedules
deploys
and manages the lifecycle of containerized workloads across a cluster of machines.

title: subnet
definition: A logical partition of an IP network that groups addresses so routers can forward traffic between isolated
addressable segments.

title: mock
definition: A test double that simulates the behavior of a dependency and verifies that the code under test calls it as expected.

title: telemetry
definition: The automated collection and transmission of metrics
traces
and logs from a running system to a central analysis backend.

title: pipeline
definition: An automated sequence of build
test
and deployment stages that moves a code change from commit to production without manual intervention.

title: index
definition: A secondary data structure that maps column values to row locations so the database can satisfy queries without scanning every table row.

title: authentication
definition: The process of verifying the identity of a user
service
or device before the system grants access to protected resources.

title: idempotency
definition: A property of an operation that produces the same final result whether it runs once or multiple times with the same input.

title: autoscaling
definition: A mechanism that automatically increases or decreases the number of running instances in response to measured load or schedule.

title: hydration
definition: The process in which a client browser attaches event handlers and interactive state to server-rendered HTML so the page becomes fully interactive.

title: rebase
definition: An operation that moves a branch's commits onto the tip of another branch so the project history stays linear and free of merge commits.

title: eviction
definition: The policy by which a cache removes stored entries when it reaches its size limit or when entries exceed their configured time to live.

title: broker
definition: A middleware server that receives messages from producers and routes them to the correct consumers while buffering them during outages.

title: pagination
definition: A response strategy that splits a large collection of records into numbered or cursor-based pages so clients fetch data in bounded
predictable chunks.

title: latency
definition: The elapsed time between a system receiving a request and returning the first or last byte of the corresponding response.

title: rollout
definition: The controlled procedure that releases a new software version to production
often in stages
so failures affect only a limited portion of traffic.

title: structured log
definition: A log entry emitted as machine-readable key-value fields instead of free text so automated systems can parse
filter
and aggregate it reliably.

title: race condition
definition: A defect that occurs when two or more concurrent operations access shared state without synchronization and the result depends on their unpredictable execution order.

title: cipher
definition: An algorithm that transforms plaintext into ciphertext and back using a key so that only parties with the key can read the protected data.

title: alert
definition: A notification fired when a metric crosses a defined threshold so an operator can investigate or a runbook can trigger an automated remediation.
